title: Ramayana: Part One earns more in its second weekend than its first, trackers estimate
dek: Nitesh Tiwari's film collected about Rs 196 crore net in India from Friday to Sunday, taking its estimated domestic total past Rs 760 crore. The makers have not published figures.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ramayana: Part One, the Nitesh Tiwari epic starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, collected an estimated Rs 196 crore net in India across all languages over its second weekend, more than the Rs 174 crore it made over its first Friday-to-Sunday weekend, according to estimates from a box-office tracker reported on Monday.

The film earned about Rs 48.10 crore on Friday, Rs 72.90 crore on Saturday and Rs 75 crore on Sunday, its 11th day in cinemas, the estimates show. That took its India net total to about Rs 760.60 crore and its estimated worldwide gross to about Rs 1,384.50 crore, including about Rs 475.50 crore overseas. The producers have not released official figures, and tracker estimates are often revised.

## How it compares

Reports differ on where the weekend ranks. One report said the all-language Rs 196 crore was the biggest second weekend recorded for an Indian film, ahead of Dhurandhar 2's Rs 172.70 crore. Another report, counting only the Hindi version, which made an estimated Rs 145.25 crore over the weekend, placed it second in Hindi cinema behind Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge at Rs 158.50 crore.

On the estimates, the film is now seventh on the all-time list of Indian films by domestic net collection, just behind RRR at about Rs 782.20 crore, and fifth worldwide, one report said.

The Hindi version accounts for most of the takings, about Rs 599.25 crore, or roughly four-fifths of the domestic net. The dubbed versions have made about Rs 48.15 crore in Kannada, Rs 42.25 crore in Telugu, Rs 36.85 crore in Tamil and Rs 34.10 crore in Malayalam, according to the same estimates.

## Background

The film, which opened on Thursday, 5 November, is the first of two parts, produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations. Its first week ran into the Diwali holidays, with its biggest single day, about Rs 107.5 crore, on Monday, 9 November, according to tracker estimates. It passed Rs 500 crore net in India in its first week and Rs 1,000 crore worldwide in eight days, according to trackers. The Bombay High Court has granted the makers a dynamic injunction against websites offering pirated copies.

A second weekend that is stronger than the first is unusual for a big release, whose takings usually fall after the opening, and more so here because the first weekend fell in the Diwali holiday period.

## What happens next

The film's weekday collections this week, the first without holiday crowds, will show whether it can pass RRR's domestic total of about Rs 782 crore, which it needs roughly Rs 22 crore more to overtake on current estimates.
